chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
When something comes out from the deceased after having been shrouded, and it hits the shroud, it should be cut off from it.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if something comes out of the deceased after shrouding?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi highlights the practical application of *taharah* (purity) in funerary rites, ensuring the deceased remains ritually clean for the afterlife. Shia jurists emphasize that only the specific area touched by the impurity is removed, preserving the integrity of the rest of the shroud, which reflects the meticulous care given to the body of the deceased.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When something comes out from the deceased after having been shrouded, and it hits the shroud, it should be cut off from it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from certain persons of his people who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If after shrouding a certain part of it (cloth) becomes unclean, it must be cut off and disposed.’”
